prd_quality.notes: The end-state PRD is exceptionally comprehensive in WHAT the system should do (28 sections covering every conceivable subsystem) and the universal business primitive taxonomy (Tab 11) is genuinely novel and well-structured. The MVP PRD is well-scoped with clear non-goals. However, specificity drops significantly when moving from 'what' to 'how' — there are no wireframes, no API contracts, no specific UI component specs, no data flow diagrams. Actionability suffers because much of the document is aspirational end-state vision mixed with current-system audits, making it hard to extract buildable user stories. The biological/Reality Mimicry metaphors (Tab 12) are intellectually rich but add no engineering specificity. The strongest actionable content is the MVP data model (Tab 1 section 11), the universal primitive taxonomy (Tab 11), and the EA gap analysis (Tab 9). The weakest areas are pricing/monetization (completely absent), UX specifics (no wireframes or interaction patterns), and competitive positioning. The document would benefit from separating the vision document from the buildable spec — right now they're interleaved across multiple tabs with significant redundancy (End-State PRD appears twice in Tab 1, substrate audit appears 3 times in Tab 15, Reality Mimicry content duplicated in Tab 12).

The document is extremely comprehensive in breadth — 12 full systems defined with detailed feature tables, data models, API endpoints, and infrastructure specs. However, it suffers from significant redundancy and internal contradictions due to being built iteratively through conversation. The same concepts (MVP scope, tech stack, database schema, API spec) are defined 2-4 times with minor variations, making it unclear which version is canonical. The full-version PRD (Systems 1-22) is well-structured and thorough. The MVP definition is inconsistent across its multiple appearances. Tab 8's ecosystem architecture is visionary but entirely conceptual — no implementation contracts. The Build Guide (pos 674944+) is the most actionable section but references yet another auth provider (Clerk) that contradicts the main PRD. Overall: strong vision, strong feature definition, but needs a single canonical pass to resolve contradictions, pick definitive tech choices, and consolidate the 3+ MVP definitions into one.

Extremely thorough product specification - one of the most detailed PRDs seen. Every onboarding question, every data model field, every hex color code, every XP calculation formula is specified. Specificity is exceptional with exact SQL schemas, component styles, and animation timings. However, actionability is lowered by: (1) significant version conflicts between PRD v1.0 (4 tabs, 3 models) and v2.0 (5 tabs, 5 models) coexisting in the same document, (2) timeline inconsistencies across sections, (3) massive content repetition across tabs (the same onboarding spec appears 3+ times in different formats), (4) missing error handling, offline behavior, and operational specs, (5) Tabs 52-53 describe an aspirational ecosystem architecture that is conceptual only with no implementation path. The document would benefit from a single canonical MVP spec with all conflicts resolved. The isolated MVP at lyfeos.net demonstrates that the core spec IS executable - the implementation proved the MVP PRD works. The ecosystem architecture (LYFEOS + EntrepreneurOS + CreatorOS on shared kernel) is compelling but currently at whiteboard stage only.
